skill.name: shar-production-metadata-validation
skill.description: Validate rights-aware AI-hybrid video-production metadata with SHAR Production's local, read-only MCP tool before delivery or release.
skill.summary: Check production manifests for required metadata and a deterministic release-readiness result.
skill.author: sharproduction

security_audit.summary: All six external-command detections are false positives because they occur in Markdown installation or client-configuration examples, not executable skill logic. The two network detections and the reconnaissance detection are also false positives; the skill states that validation is local, read-only, and does not make network requests.

remediation.issue: Installation examples contain shell commands and a repository URL that can trigger generic marketplace scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep installation commands clearly labeled as user-run setup instructions and retain the explicit statement that runtime validation performs no network access.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks on line 8 mark inline documentation terms, and the same line explicitly says the validator does not modify files or make network requests. No executable command is present.
Line 12 begins a fenced Markdown block containing user-run installation instructions. A documented git clone is not execution by the skill itself.
The detected text is the closing portion of a fenced installation example. It does not represent runtime command execution by the validator.
Line 22 begins a fenced JSON client-configuration example, not a shell execution path. The content only documents how a user configures an MCP client.
The detected text is the closing portion of the client-configuration example. It contains no command execution performed by the skill.
The backticks on line 29 format an MCP tool name and field names in prose. The line describes validation output and does not execute an external command.
Line 8 mentions that the validator does not make network requests. This is a security boundary statement, not use of a Python HTTP library.
The URL on line 13 is a public repository address in a user-run installation example. The skill does not fetch it during validation.
Line 3 is frontmatter describing a local read-only metadata validator. It contains no system inspection instruction or reconnaissance behavior.

content.value_statement: Production teams need a consistent way to catch missing or invalid manifest metadata before delivery. This skill invokes a local read-only MCP validator and explains its deterministic release-readiness result.
actual_capabilities: Identifies missing or invalid fields in a production manifest.
Presents validation errors for manifest review.
Supports rights-aware metadata checks for AI-hybrid video production.
limitations: It does not publish, deliver, or modify production assets.
It does not access credentials or make network requests during validation.
A passing result is not legal advice or rights clearance.
Validation depends on the installed MCP server and its defined rules.

use_cases.title: Review a Release Manifest
use_cases.description: Check required metadata before delivering an AI-hybrid video production package.

use_cases.title: Gate Production Handoffs
use_cases.description: Run a consistent metadata check before transferring assets between production teams.

use_cases.title: Audit Rights Metadata
use_cases.description: Inspect rights-aware manifest fields before a stakeholder reviews release readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Manifest Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this production manifest for required metadata and report whether it is releasable: [paste manifest].

prompt_templates.title: Explain Validation Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this production manifest and group each returned error by the field that needs correction: [paste manifest].

prompt_templates.title: Review a Handoff Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this handoff manifest before delivery. State the releasable result, list every error, and identify the responsible metadata area: [paste manifest].

prompt_templates.title: Assess Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the production metadata validator on this manifest. Summarize release readiness, separate blocking errors from informational context, and note that validation is not legal clearance: [paste manifest].

output_examples.input: A production manifest is missing the required delivery date.
output_examples.output: Releasable: no. Error: delivery date is required. Add the delivery date, then validate the manifest again.

output_examples.input: A complete manifest is submitted for validation.
output_examples.output: Releasable: yes. No validation errors were returned. This result does not provide legal advice or rights clearance.

output_examples.input: A manifest contains several invalid rights metadata fields.
output: Errors identify the invalid rights metadata fields.
Correct the listed fields before treating the package as ready.

best_practices: Provide factual production metadata from the current package.
Review every returned error before delivery or release.
Treat a passing result as validation evidence, not legal clearance.
anti_patterns: Do not submit invented, incomplete, or stale production metadata.
Do not treat releasable as permission to publish an asset.
Do not bypass validation errors by removing required fields.

faq.question: What does this skill validate?
faq.answer: It validates required production metadata and returns the MCP validator's releasable result with any errors.

faq.question: Does it modify my files?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses a local read-only validator and does not modify files or production assets.

faq.question: Does it make network requests?
faq.answer: No. Runtime validation is described as local and does not make network requests.

faq.question: Is a passing result legal clearance?
faq.answer: No. A passing result is not legal advice, rights clearance, or permission to publish.

faq.question: What input does the validator require?
faq.answer: Call validate_production_manifest with one object field named manifest containing the production metadata.

faq.question: Who benefits from this skill?
faq.answer: Video producers, post-production coordinators, and rights specialists can use it before delivery or release.
